subject: Product title / training rights clarifications for Acme Order Form
messages:
From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmeretail.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmeretail.com
Date: Sat, 22 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on IP / training rights in Order Form v3

Hi Hannah,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our procurement/legal team reviewed the latest Order Form (v3) and came back with a few IP-related questions we need to resolve before we can route to execs for signature. High-level items:

1) Output ownership: The Order Form and MSA currently reference "Customer outputs" but don't explicitly state whether those outputs can be used by Redwood for model improvements. Our priority is to ensure Acme retains title to customer outputs and that Redwood's use for model training is opt-in.

2) Feedback/telemetry: We expect telemetry necessary for service operation (latency, error rates) but want any feedback license scoped narrowly — e.g., aggregated/anonymized telemetry only for product improvement, no re-training or derivative model creation from our data.

3) Data retention / access logs: We need confirmation about retention windows and whether audit logs (who queried what) can be provided for compliance reviews.

I've attached a short Q&A doc and a redline (tracked comments) of the Order Form to this email. Could you loop in the appropriate legal contact at Redwood? If possible, we would like a short synchronous call next week to resolve these points.

Attachments: Acme_IP_Qs_20270522.docx; Acme_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Counsel, Acme Retail
emma.jones@acmeretail.com
+1 512-555-0192

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 23 May 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on IP / training rights in Order Form v3

Emma — thanks for the clear summary and for the redlines. Looping in Ben (AE) and Evelyn (senior counsel) so we can get legal review and a proposed set of acceptable edits.

Couple quick clarifying Qs from me before Evelyn drafts language:
- For "output ownership": when you say "retain title," do you need an absolute assignment clause, or would a clear statement that Redwood "does not claim ownership" of customer-provided content and direct outputs suffice?
- For the feedback license scope: is Acme comfortable with a time-bound opt-in mechanism (customer can separately opt a workspace into model-improvement) or do you require a blanket prohibition in the MSA/Order Form?

We'll aim to provide proposed redline language and a short mutual action plan by EOD Monday so you have something concrete for your execs. Happy to set a 30-minute call Tuesday afternoon — does 2pm PT work?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Enterprise Sales Lead, Redwood Inference
Signature: Redwood Inference | hannah_s@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0104

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on IP / training rights in Order Form v3

Emma — thanks for the detailed note and the redlines. I've done an initial pass and propose the following approach to preserve both parties' needs:

1) Output ownership: Insert a short clause to the Order Form: "Customer retains title to Customer Content and Outputs. Redwood will not claim ownership of Customer Content or Outputs." That addresses the "title" ask while avoiding a full assignment that complicates downstream licensing.

2) Feedback / training: Add a two-tier mechanism:
   - Operational telemetry (logs, metrics, errors) is permitted and scoped to service operation and troubleshooting.
   - Model training / improvement from Customer Content or Outputs requires an explicit Opt-In checkbox at the workspace level and will be governed by a separate Data Use Addendum.

3) Data retention & audit logs: Standard retention is 90 days for request/response payloads by default; audit logs (who queried what) are retained for 365 days. We can offer an extended retention add-on on Dedicated/Private deployments and carve-outs for compliance review with an SLA for export requests.

I'll attach a tracked-redline of the Order Form with these edits and a short mutual action plan for signatures and escalation. Ben / Hannah — please review commercial impacts, esp. any revenue/discount implications if the customer opts out of training.

Attachments: Draft_OrderForm_v3_with_EDITS.pdf; Draft_Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx

Regards,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmeretail.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@acmeretail.com
Date: Wed, 25 May 2027 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on IP / training rights in Order Form v3

Evelyn / Hannah — appreciate the quick turnaround and the pragmatic split on telemetry vs training. Our internal counsel reviewed your proposed language and provided a couple of counterpoints in the attached PDF (redlines):

- We can accept the "no claim of ownership" language for Outputs.
- We need explicit language that Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to build derivative models that are made available to other customers, regardless of opt-in status, unless Acme signs the Data Use Addendum. (Concern: downstream commercialized models.)
- For audit logs: confirm whether exports include the full request/response or only metadata; we need full request/response in a secure export for compliance reviews (sensitive PII redaction would be Acme's responsibility).

We are ok with the workspace-level opt-in model for training, but want a contractual guarantee that without opt-in Redwood will never persist training datasets derived from Acme to long-term model tuning stores.

Attachment: Acme_OrderForm_v3_redlines.pdf

We are available for the Tuesday 2pm PT slot you suggested to iron out remaining line edits.

Thanks,
Emma Jones
Counsel, Acme Retail

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Emma Jones <emma.jones@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 May 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Questions on IP / training rights in Order Form v3

Emma — thanks, that is helpful and actionable. Next steps per our internal alignment:

- Evelyn will revise the redline to add explicit non-derivative language you requested ("Redwood will not use Customer Content or Outputs to produce derivative models available to other customers absent a signed Data Use Addendum").
- We'll confirm the exact export scope for audit logs (full request/response vs metadata) and propose secure delivery options (SFTP with encryption or KMS-wrapped export).
- Ben / I will confirm whether there is any commercial impact to opt-out on training (likely a modest uplift on unit pricing if training opt-out is chosen) and circulate a short commercial note before our call.

Can you confirm the 2pm PT slot on Tuesday for a 30 minute call? If so we'll send a calendar invite and a one-page agenda.

Appreciate the collaboration — we want to keep this simple for both sides.

Best,
